## Decisions

- ⏳ **open** `i-no-design-anchor` `medium confidence` (scaffold): Spectrum ships no Icon component set in Figma, so this contract has code evidence only. Accept a code-first contract, or wait for a design anchor that may never exist? _Evidence: S2 / Web lists 142 component sets and none is Icon._
  - The draft chose: accepted code-first; anchors.figma.kind is "none"
  - If wrong: If Spectrum later publishes an Icon set, re-anchor and re-extract.
- ⏳ **open** `i-scale-axis` `medium confidence` (Matt): Spectrum's tokens carry a scale axis (medium and large) that S2A does not have; the same token resolves to 20px and 24px. Which scale does adobe.com bind to? _Evidence: @spectrum-css/tokens 16.0.2 medium-vars.css and large-vars.css_
  - The draft chose: medium, matching desktop web
  - If wrong: If a surface needs large scale, the token directory gains a second mode rather than the contract gaining a prop.
- ⏳ **open** `i-host-rules` `high confidence` (Matt): Every rule in the icon stylesheet is :host or ::slotted — there is not one class in it. _Evidence: icon-base.css is :host, :host([size]), and svg,::slotted(*) only. The class is ours, which is why the anatomy cannot be checked against the stylesheet._
  - The draft chose: Declare swc-Icon as the root class and re-express the host rules on it
  - If wrong: If the generated component becomes a custom element, drop the class and inherit the host rules.
- ✅ decided `i-implementation` `high confidence` (Matt): Which package is Spectrum 2's Icon? → The contract describes @adobe/spectrum-wc. Icon has no module of its own beyond a slot and a size box; its stylesheet is shared, at dist/stylesheets/_lit-styles/icon-base.js. _Evidence: Icon.js imports icon-base.js for its only styles and renders a single default slot._
  - The draft chose: @adobe/spectrum-wc (swc-icon)
  - If wrong: none
- ✅ decided `i-override-seam` `high confidence` (Matt): How does a consumer resize or recolour the icon? → Upstream exposes three custom properties on the host and derives everything else from them, so the size prop and a direct override reach the same place. _Evidence: icon-base.css declares all three on :host with the size attribute switching the first two._
  - The draft chose: --swc-icon-inline-size, --swc-icon-block-size and --swc-icon-color
  - If wrong: none
- ✅ decided `i-glyph-fill` `high confidence` (Matt): Every glyph rendered in its own colour instead of the component's. → Spectrum's workflow SVGs paint with fill="var(--iconPrimary, #222)" rather than currentColor, so with nothing defining that property every glyph fell back to #222 regardless of the colour around it. Setting --iconPrimary to currentColor on the icon part makes a glyph follow its component, and leaves the property available to anyone who wants a different colour. _Evidence: All 396 entries in spectrum-icons.json carry var(--iconPrimary, #222); all 26 in our own s2a-icons.json use currentColor. Measured: the badge's text was #ffffff while its glyph painted #222222._
  - The draft chose: Map the artwork's own hook to currentColor on the part that holds the glyph
  - If wrong: none. The alternative was rewriting 396 vendored SVGs, which would mean editing artwork we do not own.

## Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA: `1.1.1`

- Decorative by default: the root sets pointer-events none and the glyph carries no accessible name.
- A meaningful icon needs a name on the element that owns the meaning, not on the glyph.
